title: Windows and Doors Rebates in Vaughan 2026: A Young City and the $100 Rebate
desc: Vaughan window and door rebates for 2026: $100 per rough opening, in the Ontario city with the lowest share of pre-1981 homes (8%) in our data.
h1: Windows and Doors Rebates in Vaughan
lead: Vaughan has the youngest housing in our Ontario set: just 8% of its 103,910 households live in a home built before 1981. For most Vaughan owners the window rebate is not the first upgrade to price.
cards_heading: What the Home Renovation Savings program pays for windows and doors in Vaughan
cards_intro: We re-read the program's page and its eligibility requirements on October 3, 2026. Windows and doors are paid only inside the assessment stream, so every amount here comes with an assessment and at least two upgrades.

cards.title: Windows and doors
cards.note: One payment per opening in an outside wall, not per unit. A bay window with three panes in one opening earns $100.

cards.title: Smallest qualifying job
cards.note: Three window openings, or one door, sliding door or skylight opening, count as one qualified measure. Two windows alone earn nothing.

cards.title: Home energy assessment
cards.note: $600 comes back when the program is completed. Covers the cost of the first and the follow-up assessment once the program is completed.

cards.title: Three or more upgrades
cards.note: Windows count as one upgrade. Insulation, air sealing and a heat pump water heater are the others in this stream.

cards.title: Program cap
cards.note: $10,000 for homes heated by electricity, oil, propane or wood, and $5,000 for homes heated by Enbridge gas.

after_cards: The program is run by Enbridge Gas and Save on Energy. Post-audits must be scheduled by November 30, 2026 and completed by December 31, 2026, or within 180 days of your first assessment, whichever comes first.
sections: Why this page starts with a warning

Of Vaughan's 103,910 households, 86% own and 81% live in an eligible house type, but only 4,890 are owner-occupied detached houses built before 1981. Roughly 20% of households live in homes built since 2011. The program requires replacing windows that are not ENERGY STAR certified, so owners of newer homes often have nothing to replace for the rebate.
Where windows may still make sense

Homes from the 1980s and 1990s may have windows that are decades old. Check the manufacturer label. If your windows are already ENERGY STAR certified but have failed seals, fogging or drafts, replacement may still be worthwhile for comfort, though the rebate will not apply to windows that were already certified.
Rebates that may matter more here

With a young stock and a low major-repairs rate (2.5%), insulation and heating are the more common upgrades. The assessment stream pays up to $1,500 for an attic and $500 for a heat pump water heater, and the single-upgrade stream pays up to $7,500 for a cold-climate heat pump. Use the window rebate only if the audit shows real heat loss at the openings.

About 13% of Vaughan households live in apartments of five or more storeys. Those households are not eligible for Home Renovation Savings. Owners in condo buildings should ask their board what the building plans for window replacement, since that is a common-element decision.
What the audit actually tells you

The first assessment includes a blower door test and a report on where the house leaks. In a newer Vaughan home the report may show that windows are not the weak point, with attic hatches, rim joists and wall penetrations leaking more. Take the report seriously: a program that pays $100 per opening is a nudge, not a reason to replace sound windows. If the audit finds little to fix, you will have spent $600 up front and received it back only if you complete the program.
claim_steps: Confirm you own the home, it has been occupied for six months and it is one of the eligible house types.
Book the first home energy assessment with a registered energy advisor before any work starts.
Choose at least one more upgrade to pair with the windows, and get quotes that count rough openings the way the program does.
Read the manufacturer label before you assume the windows need replacing.
Have a professional install complete windows or doors with frames, keep the ENERGY STAR labels on until the follow-up assessment, and book it.
faq: Does Vaughan have many older houses?
Fewer than any other Ontario city in our data: 8% of households live in homes built before 1981.
Are my 1990s windows eligible for replacement?
Only if they are not ENERGY STAR certified. The program requires replacing non-certified models.
$10,000 for electric, oil, propane or wood, $5,000 for Enbridge gas.
